cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: I Need Your Blessing
cards.instruction: Get approval from someone whose opinion still carries emotional weight, even when permission is unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Mum, we signed the lease. Say it's good news before I open the wine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need my permission to move in with Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I know. I still want my mother to be pleased.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm pleased for you. I'm still getting used to Sam.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you toast both of us? I want to remember you welcoming our home, not just tolerating my address.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 orders good news and stock prefixes claim rank, but A3 want mother pleased and A5 could you toast do not sustain a distinct superior approval tactic.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 permission unnecessary prompts A3 emotional distinction; B4 partial pleasure prompts A5 request for joint welcome, a coherent need.

relationship.evidence: B2 recognizes autonomy and B4 is honest about adjusting to Sam, giving A partial support rather than simple rejection.

heightening.evidence: B4 pleased for A but unsure of Sam causes A5 a toast to both and the shared home, deepening rather than repeating the blessing request.

specificity.evidence: A1 signed lease and wine establish celebration; B2 move with Sam and A3 mother define why her opinion matters.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 welcoming home versus tolerating address is pointed but the added decision phrases are tonally detached.
